title: Vedanta (revisited)
hook: a father's short line to his son, "you are that", and three great teachers who hear it three ways

segments.voice: Yesterday, Vedanta pointed: Brahman as that from which the world is born, like a branch showing the moon.
screen: `THE BRANCH AND THE MOON.` · `ONE LINE, THREE HEARINGS.`

segments.voice: Tat tvam asi. You are that. A father says it to his son in the Chandogya Upanishad, again and again, after showing him salt dissolved in water and a seed split open to nothing you can see. And here is the surprise. Three of Vedanta's great teachers, Shankara, Ramanuja and Madhva, each honor this line and build on it, and they don't hear it the same way. Same words, same Upanishad, same Brahma Sutra underneath. Today each of the three reads the line aloud.
screen: `TAT TVAM ASI.` → `ONE LINE EVERYONE HONORS.` → `THREE TEACHERS AT ONE TABLE.`

segments.voice: Shankara reads it straight. You, at your deepest, are Brahman. Not part of it, not near it. Advaita teaching offers an image: the sense of being a separate little self is like the space inside a clay pot. Break the pot and nothing goes anywhere; the space was never two. His school is called Advaita, not-two. Ramanuja reads the same line and keeps the self real. In the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad, the sage Yajnavalkya speaks of the one who dwells within all things, whom the things don't know, whose body they are, who guides them from inside. For Ramanuja, that's the key. The world and every self are like Brahman's body. A body is truly real, truly yours, and never apart from you. So you are that, the way a body belongs wholly to the one who lives in it. His school is called Vishishtadvaita. Madhva reads the line and hears difference. For him, Brahman, whom he knows as Vishnu, and the self are always two, and the self is wholly dependent, like a reflection that's real, but only because something shines. The line, read his way, speaks of closeness and likeness, never sameness. His school is called Dvaita, two. Three readings, each one argued with care from the same texts. Hindus who follow each line keep reading, praying and living by it to this day. The darshanas are never ranked here, and neither are these.
screen: `SHANKARA: NEVER TWO.` · `RAMANUJA: THE WORLD AS GOD'S BODY.` · `MADHVA: ALWAYS TWO, ALWAYS CLOSE.` · `THREE READINGS, NONE RANKED.`

segments.voice: Let the words come quietly, you are that, and hear them first as Shankara might, resting as the open space the pot never divided; then as Ramanuja might, feeling yourself held from inside, the way a body belongs to the one who lives in it; then as Madhva might, noticing that you didn't make yourself shine. Give each a few breaths, and you don't have to choose. If you pray, you can let the line rest in the name you pray to.
Vedanta. Today, the line you are that, heard as not-two, as body and soul, and as two who stay close. Today's word.
Your line: Vedanta, revisited. One line, three readings, none ranked. Same time tomorrow.

howItsDone: Hindus in the Advaita, Vishishtadvaita and Dvaita lines each study the Upanishads through their own teacher's commentary, Shankara's, Ramanuja's or Madhva's, and the line tat tvam asi is read and taught in each lineage in its own way.

original.note: Sanskrit: you are that, from the Chandogya Upanishad, read differently by each Vedanta school.

trapdoor: what you thought: tat tvam asi means one thing in Hinduism.
what it means: the great Vedanta teachers honor the same line and read it as not-two, as body and soul, or as two who stay close.
what a scholar hears: Chandogya 6.8.7 and after, read by Advaita, Vishishtadvaita and Dvaita, with Ramanuja leaning on the inner controller of Brihadaranyaka 3.7.

chat.says: Do all Vedanta teachers agree on what 'you are that' means?
options: No: Shankara hears not-two, Ramanuja body and soul, Madhva two who stay close.
Yes, every teacher reads it as saying the self and Brahman are identical.
Yes, all three read it as a line about salt and seeds, not about the self.
chat.meaning: Shankara, Ramanuja and Madhva each honor tat tvam asi and hear it differently: not-two, the world as God's body, and always two.

Tat tvam asi.meaning: you are that: a father's teaching in the Chandogya Upanishad

Vishishtadvaita.meaning: Ramanuja's school: the world and selves as Brahman's body

Madhva.meaning: the teacher for whom Brahman and the self are always two

sources.ref: Chandogya Upanishad 6.8.7–6.16 (Uddalaka to Shvetaketu: you are that; salt in water; the seed)
Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 3.7 (the inner controller, whose body all things are)
Shankara, Ramanuja and Madhva on Chandogya 6.8.7 and on the Brahma Sutra

notes: The pot-space image (ghatakasha) is standard in Advaita teaching; confirm it fits Shankara rather than only later Advaita.
Ramanuja's body-soul reading (sharira-shariri bhava) and use of Brihadaranyaka 3.7: confirm.

Madhva's reading: the script says only that he hears closeness and likeness, never sameness, and uses the reflection image (pratibimba). Some in his line read the sandhi as 'atat tvam asi'; deliberately left out. A Dvaita Keeper should check the framing.
The salt and seed teachings in Chandogya 6 are paraphrased and ordered loosely; confirm.
